entries.title: Report Builder: filter and sort by reviewer recommendation
entries.summary: In a Sessions report, **Reviewer recommendation** (Accept, Decline or Alternate) and **Reviewer recommendation note** are now under **Reviews** in the Fields panel. They filter and sort, and on one row per session they count each recommendation, so a report can list every session a reviewer marked Alternate.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Reviews → Reviewer recommendation

entries.use_case: Program teams that triage with reviewer recommendations can pull Accept, Decline and Alternate straight into a report, count them per session and filter to the Alternates, instead of building a rubric question to copy the call.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says the Recommendation column in Report Builder is blank, or asks how to report on reviewers' Accept / Decline / Alternate calls.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using reviewer recommendations (the Accept / Decline / Alternate feature on a review plan round) who also uses Report Builder.
internal.staff_path: Reports → Report Builder → add a Reviews column → Reviewer recommendation
internal.gotchas: Reads the round's Recommendation feature, not a rubric question labelled 'Recommendation'. A rubric workaround question still shows in its own column. A recommendation the reviewer removed stops showing.
internal.talk_track: If your reviewers recommend Accept, Decline or Alternate in a round, those calls are now report columns you can filter and count.

entries.title: Campaign preview counts only the contacts you picked
entries.summary: An email campaign that holds hand-picked contacts (one copied or duplicated with its picked contacts) now previews and counts exactly those contacts on **Preview as…**, the same people it sends to, instead of everyone in the event. When **Review** on a Send Email can't build a preview, the reason the server gave is shown with the error.
entries.use_case: The preview and count now match who will actually get a duplicated hand-picked campaign, so organizers can trust the number before they send.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that a duplicated campaign's preview listed far more people than it was sent to, or that Review failed with no reason.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who send from selected records and duplicate those campaigns.
internal.staff_path: Event → Communications → Email Campaigns → open campaign → Preview
internal.gotchas: Sending was always correct; only the preview list and count were wrong.

entries.title: Speakers who sign in at the organizer login are pointed to their portal
entries.summary: A speaker, submitter or reviewer who signs in at the organizer login with no organization to open no longer hits a bare **No organizations found**. The page explains that their drafts and submissions are in the event's portal, reached from the event's email or the submission form, shows the email they are signed in with, and offers **Sign out**.

where.path: Organizer login → home page, signed in without an organization

entries.use_case: Speakers who land in the wrong place now see where to go, which saves a support email for the organizer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer forwards a speaker's 'No organizations found' screenshot.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer with external submitters or speakers.
internal.staff_path: Sign in at the admin login as a contact with no organization access
internal.gotchas: The fix is the explanation; the person still has to open the portal link from the event's email or submission form.

entries.title: Link preview text for a Site
entries.summary: The Site builder has a **Link preview** setting under **Social share image**: the text shown under the Site's name when its link is pasted into Slack, LinkedIn or Teams (up to 300 characters), with a preview card beside it. Left empty, the card uses the landing **Subtitle** as before.

where.path: Sites → open a Site → Settings → Site → Link preview

entries.use_case: Organizers can write the text a shared Site link shows without changing the subtitle visitors see on the landing page.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to change the text Slack or LinkedIn shows for their Site link.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who share Awards or program Site links on social or in Slack.
internal.staff_path: Org → Sites → Site → Settings → Site → Link preview
internal.gotchas: Takes effect after Publish. Slack and LinkedIn cache previews of links they have already seen for a while.

entries.title: SSO-only Sites publish without opening Login / SSO first
entries.summary: A Site with **SSO Login** as its only sign-in method could refuse to publish with **Select at least one identity provider or disable SSO login** after a reload, unless you opened **Login / SSO** first. **Publish** now checks the identity providers linked to the Site, so a duplicated SSO-only Site publishes straight away.
entries.use_case: Organizers who duplicate an SSO-only Site for a new season can publish it without a confusing error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports the identity-provider error on publish although SSO is set up.
internal.gotchas: The error is still correct when no provider is linked to the Site.

entries.title: Adding a new speaker works again on events with Gleanin
entries.summary: On events with Gleanin connected, adding a **new** contact to a session (the **Add contact** panel) failed with **Request failed**. It works again; adding an existing contact was not affected.
entries.use_case: Organizers on Gleanin-connected events can add brand-new speakers to sessions again.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Gleanin customer reported 'Request failed' adding a speaker in mid-November.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → session → Participants → Add → new contact
internal.gotchas: Broke with the 2026-11-15 release; fixed in the next deploy.
